facts.label: Recent violations
facts.text: None in the 12 quarters from July 2023 to June 2026.

facts.label: Violations on record
facts.text: 3, from 2011 and 2017. None was health-based, and all are marked as returned to compliance.

facts.label: Lead at the tap
facts.text: 0.002 mg/L at the 90th percentile of the homes sampled in 2025. EPA's action level is 0.015 mg/L.

facts.label: Sources
facts.text: 4 active surface-water intakes and 54 active wells (134 wells on record, 80 of them inactive).

facts.label: PFAS
facts.text: Detected in 19 of 522 results from the system's plants in 2024. The highest were PFOA at 7.5 ng/L and PFOS at 6.8 ng/L, both at the Stony Brook Plant. New Jersey's limits are 14 and 13 ng/L. EPA's 2024 rule sets 4.0 ng/L for each, with compliance required at a later date (2029 in the rule as issued). A detection is not a violation.

caveat: These are records for the whole system, which serves many towns. They are not a test of any one tap, and they do not say the water is safe or unsafe.
